audit: Cases with diagnosis 'missing' (81) or 'Unknown' (25) were excluded, as were 10 hypermutated cases with more than 500 non-synonymous mutations (one has 15,731), which otherwise dominate gene counts. Diagnosis labels are heterogeneous and overlap (e.g. 'Glioma, malignant' vs 'Astrocytoma, NOS'); many diagnoses have fewer than 10 cases and were not tested, and the comparator is the rest of a mixed brain, sarcoma and carcinoma cohort rather than a tissue-matched group. Mutation burden varies by more than 100-fold between diagnoses (median 2 in pilocytic astrocytoma vs 24 in embryonal RMS), so burden-driven passenger hits are a risk; I re-checked the top claims with burden-stratified observed/expected ratios and most held, but this is not a full adjustment. Small groups such as craniopharyngioma (n=11), ATRT (n=27) and the NOTCH2/MED12 signals carry wide uncertainty. MED12 and NOTCH2 hits are scattered across the gene (missense, nonsense and frameshift, no hotspot), which fits passenger or gene-length effects or calling artifact. The file has no VAF, filter or germline annotation, and I did not check whether several cases come from the same patient. Ages run 0 to 25 with 81 missing, and 81 cases lack a site. Established flags come from my own recall of the literature, not from a check against sources, since I had no internet access. Expected frequencies are in-cohort rates, lightly shrunk, and are not calibrated to new patients.
methods: For each diagnosis with at least 10 cases (after excluding missing/Unknown labels and hypermutated cases), I built a 2x2 table for every gene carried by at least 3 analysed cases and tested enrichment against all other analysed cases with a one-sided hypergeometric (Fisher) test, implemented with the Python standard library. Of 244 tests with at least 3 mutated cases in the diagnosis, I controlled the false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg. I checked the top findings by computing burden-stratified observed/expected counts (strata of total mutations per case) and by restricting to cases with 20 or fewer mutations. I reported claims with a BH q-value clearly below 0.05 and a plausible biological rationale, with probabilities reflecting replication risk from small groups and passenger effects.
